outcome: Baby admission to Special Care Nursery
Baby admission to Neonatal Intensive Care Unit
cohort: A cohort of 186,789 mothers and 189,909 babies who gave birth in Queensland, Australia between 2012 and 2015, identified from linked administrative health and cost data.
finding: Mothers with diabetes during pregnancy required greater health care and resource use, experiencing higher total government expenditure, and were more likely to have adverse maternal (induced labour, C-section) and neonatal (preterm birth, SCN/NICU admission) outcomes compared to mothers without diabetes.
mod_finding: Mothers with diabetes during pregnancy were significantly more likely to have a cesarean section (OR: 1.26) compared to mothers without diabetes.
followup_time: Up to 1000 days from the start of the perinatal journey (including pregnancy and post-birth period) for cost analysis, with immediate post-birth outcomes for maternal and neonatal events.
